verdict.rationale: Better Auth stores all auth data in the integrator's own standard database (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL), so the data is already in open, directly accessible formats. Community users confirm they own their data and that the adapter design makes switching libraries relatively easy. There is no first-party export feature or documented exit or export procedure, so portability comes from the self-hosted architecture rather than a dedicated capability. missing for 10: documented first-party data export tooling, a documented migration-out / leave guide, hands-on corroboration of a full exit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Better Auth requires a database to store user data. You can easily configure Better Auth to use SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL, and more!
You get all of your auth data in your own db in 1 cli command. You are not tied to any db provider.
It just works and I own all the data.
They noted the database adapter design makes it relatively easy to switch to another provider or library.
